title: Songwriters' Workshop - Theme: "Spring"
descriptionHtml:
Hello everyone!

KickDrum and The Yellow Door/La Porte Jaune would like to present our second Songwriters' Workshop. The theme is "Spring", so bring a piece to share about this season of change and new life!

We'll start the workshop by meeting each other and then getting our creative minds flowing with a "Free-Flow" writing exercise and several other activities. After that you'll all have the chance to share a song about our weekly theme and get constructive feedback and comments from your fellow musicians.

The workshop is a weekly "community of practice" for local musicians, where we are able to talk collectively about different themes and aspects of the songwriting process.

The goal is to create a space where musicians can meet, network, share, and learn from each other through open dialogue.

title: Myles Hildebrand // Téo // Josh Spencer @ Santropol
descriptionHtml:
KickDrum is super happy to present 3 local Montréal songwriters and for an evening of music in a format not commonly seen in the city.

PLUS IT'S IN SANTROPOL'S BEAUTIFUL BACKYARD!

We're hosting a songwriters' circle, meaning that all the performers will be on stage at the same time, taking turns swapping songs, stories, and anecdotes between each other, allowing for a "realness" that you just never get in a standard show.

---

Entry is by donation (Pay-What-You-Can)

---

Myles Hildebrand (Myles from Home/ Café Racer) - Myles has spent many nights playing guitar on his balcony in downtown Montreal. In this ultra-urban setting he has created music more reminiscent of the flat prairies of Manitoba where he was born and raised.

Téo - Auteur-compositeur-interprète de Montréal, originaire de Gatineau.

Josh Spencer ( The Arborists / Birches) - Taking influences from the likes of Glen Hansard, Conor Oberst, Dan Mangan, and Bahamas, Josh's sound is a jumble of his favourite songwriters, creating pensive but powerful songs. His band "Birches" & "The Arborists" are both releasing EPs this upcoming fall.

*You are free to order drinks/food inside but please enter through the opening in the fence on Duluth. There will be seating available for you there :)

As Montréalers, and active musicians & artists, we’ve been disappointed by the lack of cultural events in the winter months, which only exacerbates the isolation and seasonal depression many of us can grapple with! So, to fight this isolation, we want to give an opportunity for artists and musicians to showcase their work in the winter, and provide great spaces for people to come together, have a warm drink, socialize, and enjoy the amazing creativity this city has to offer.

///

Qui sommes nous et c'est quoi le Marathon d'Hiver?

En tant que montréalais, artistes et musiciens, nous avons longtemps été déçus par le manque d'activités culturelles lors de la saison hibernale. Ceci ne fait qu'inciter le sentiment d'isolement et la dépression en nous! Afin de combattre cela, on veut offrir la chance aux musiciens et aux artistes de partager leur travail cet hiver dans des espaces où les gens pourront se rassembler , prendre un verre et jaser dans une ambiance créative et chaleureuse!

----

KickDrum, in collaboration with Plus 1, is proud to support USC Canada with $1 from every entry to this year's KickDrum Summer Marathon d'Été • juillet 12 - 17

However, money is only one way of lending support... so, after 4 jam-packed days of music, we are also hosting a special screening and discussion on the documentary, "The Cross of the Moment", by Jacob Freydont-Attie.

The film is a deep-green/deep-time, highly cerebral discussion of the environmental crisis, which attempts to connect the dots between Fermi’s Paradox, climate change, capitalism, and collapse.

A detailed description of the film can be found below and the trailer in the discussion section

We've invited several local environmental groups (which will be announced soon) to lead the post-screening discussion. These groups will not only lead a discussion but also give us the opportunity to get further involved in various local and national movements!

Come ready to listen and discuss. We look forward to meeting you!

----

Entry is by donation ($5 suggested)
*Proceeds will help cover the rental fee for the space

6:00pm • Doors open
6:30pm • Screening
8:00pm • Discussion

----

The Cross of the Moment
(run time • 84 min)

A deep-green/deep-time, highly cerebral discussion of the environmental crisis, The Cross of the Moment attempts to connect the dots between Fermi’s Paradox, climate change, capitalism, and collapse. Interviews with top scientists and public intellectuals are woven together into a narrative that is challenging, exhausting, and often depressing as it refuses to accept the easy answers posited by other overly-simplistic climate change documentaries. No fancy graphics or distracting introductions detract from what is essentially an 80 minute constructed conversation among a group of highly informed experts on the most important topic in human history; will our species survive catastrophic climate change? The film is divided into seven chapters that start from the widest perspective, why do we appear to be alone in the galaxy, and slowly narrows its focuses through a series of topics including Rare Earth Theory, human impact on the biosphere, potential solutions, structural barriers to implementation, the possibility of the collapse of civilization, and a final call for immediate engagement at all levels of society.

Interviewees are Don Brownlee, Roger Carasso, Robin Hanson, Mark Jacobson, Derrick Jensen, David Klein, Bill McKibben, Guy McPherson, Bill Patzert, Gary Snyder, Jill Stein, Peter Ward, and Josh Willis. Some of these are household names, other are more obscure scientists working in academia or for government institutions such as NASA. What they all share is a pressing concern for the future of our planet. Certainly more demanding on its audience than similar films, there is also present here a layer of humor and, more importantly, a deep sense of humanity. By the end the audience has not just explored our current crisis from a variety of thoughtful perspectives, but also become acquainted with these highly original intellectuals as people seeking truth as we all are.

The film takes its title from a stanza of W. H. Auden’s poem The Age of Anxiety, published in 1947.

We would rather be ruined than changed;
We would rather die in our dread
Than climb the cross of the moment
And let our illusions die.

----

KickDrum, en collaboration avec Plus 1, est fier de donner à USC Canada 1$ par entrée achetée pour le KickDrum Summer Marathon d'Été • Montréal • juillet 13 - 16.

Cependant, l’argent n’est pas la seule manière d’aider… ainsi, après 4 jours complets d’évènements musicaux nous organisons une projection et une discussion autour du film documentaire "The Cross of the Moment" de Jacob Freydont-Attie.

Ce film inspirant guide sur des pistes de réflexion poussées sur la crise environnementale, en tentant de connecter le Paradoxe Fermi, changements climatiques, capitalisme et collapse.

Une description détaillée du film se trouve au dessous et la bande annonce dans la partie discussion de l’évènement Facebook.

Nous avons invite plusieurs groupes Montréalais se dédiant à l’environnement (annoncés sous peu) pour mener la discussion d’après visionnage. Ils seront non seulement présents pour médier la discussion mais aussi pour donner l’opportunité aux spectateurs de s’engager dans les divers mouvements locaux et nationaux !

KickDrum est fier de présenter son deuxième Festival d'hiver annual ! ⛄

Organisé entièrement par des bénévoles, le festival se déroulera du jeudi 16 février au dimanche 19 février à deux endroits de Montréal: Le Cagibi au cœur du Plateau-Mont-Royal et le Café Aunja au cœur du centre-ville.

Le Festival d'hiver présentera 30 groupes musicales de partout à Montréal. De plus, 100% des profits du festival seront donnés à Jam pour la justice (jampourlajustice.org), un organisme sans but lucratif, pour soutenir ses programmes de musique. En assistant, vous serez en train de soutenir certains des meilleurs talents locaux de Montréal et des communautés dans le besoin. C'est un gagnant-gagnant pour la musique !

(VERSION FRANÇAISE CI-DESSUS)

The Winter Fetsival will feature 30 musical acts from across Montreal. Additionally, 100% of festival profits will be donated to Jam for Justice to support its music programs. title: Katalogue Montreal Launch
descriptionHtml:
Join us at Le Cagibi in celebration of the Montréal Music Scene and the launch of Katalogue; a new community resource that makes it easier than ever to discover and support local sounds

Nous vous invitons à Le Cagibi pour célébrer la scène musicale de Montréal et le lancement de Katalogue; une nouvelle ressource communautaire qui facilite la découverte et le soutien des artistes locaux.

5 à 7
Free / Gratuit

6596 St. Laurent
Montreal, Quebec H2S 3C6

---

Our Message

Montreal is home to a vibrant and dynamic music scene. This is not because of countless international festivals and touring acts, but the thousands of talented, underground, local artists who call it home.

Independent venues also contribute significantly to this atmosphere, as they provide accessible opportunities for artists to grow and showcase their work. Music performed at spaces such as Casa del Popolo and l’Esco, not the Bell Centre or MTelus, are what makes Montréal special.

However, as a consequence of climbing rental prices, an increasing number of these vital local venues are forced to move or shut down (i.e. Le Cagibi and Divan Orange). Artists that have lived in and built up the cultural capital of neighbourhoods such as the Mile End are forced out to make room for more commercial properties and international brands.

In this environment, it’s more important than ever to celebrate and support local artists… that is unless you actually want our city to resemble Toronto?

Our Inspiration

It shouldn’t be hard to find local artists you’ll love

Major streaming platforms such as Apple Music and Spotify don’t give listeners the option to browse artists by location, and only offer limited playlist options associated with certain cities. That means if you want to listen local, you ’ll have to ask around, google away, sift through niche media, or dig through local event listings. It should be easy to discover music being created in your own backyard!

So, we’ve done all the hard work for you and have compiled a growing list of over 1,100 local artists and bands into one place.

Discover music you’ll love through browsing, listening to our curated playlists, searching through a variety of different genre tags, or by checking out our local concert listings!

---

Notre mission

Qu’écouter localement devienne simple et passionnant.

Notre message

Montréal abrite une scène musicale vibrante et dynamique. Ceci n’est pas dû aux nombreux festivals et tournées internationaux, mais plutôt aux artistes locaux talentueux et « underground » qui y habitent.

Les salles indépendantes contribuent énormément à l’atmosphère musicale de Montréal, car elles offrent à nos artistes des opportunités accessibles pour se faire connaitre et se développer. C’est la musique jouée dans les espaces comme la Casa del Popolo et l’Escogriffe, et non au Centre Bell ou MTelus, qui rend Montréal unique.

Cependant, dû aux hausses des prix de locations, plusieurs de ses salles indépendantes sont obligés de fermer ou de se déplacer (i.e. Divan Orange et le Cagibi). Les artistes ayant vécus et contribués à la construction la notre capitale culturelle de quartiers comme le Mile End sont obligés de donner place aux propriétés commerciales et marques internationales.

Dans un environnement comme le notre, célébrer et supporter nos artistes locaux est d’une importance majeure… à moins que vous vouliez vivre dans une ville comme Toronto?

Notre inspiration

Trouver des artistes locaux que vous aimez ne devrait pas être difficile.

Les principales plateformes de diffusion telle que Spotify et Apple Music ne permettent pas aux auditeurs de parcourir les artistes par localisation, et ne permettent que quelques options de playlists associées à certaines villes. Ceci veut dire que si vous désirez écouter de la musique locale, vous devez chercher indirectement – sur google, les médias de niche, bouche à oreille, ou les listes d’évènements locaux. Découvrir de la musique créée dans ta propre arrière-cour ne devrait pas être si difficile!

Donc, nous avons travaillé fort pour vous en compilant une liste croissante de plus de 1,000 artistes et groupes de musique locaux à un endroit!

Découvrez de la musique que vous aimerez en naviguant, en écoutant nos listes de lecture organisées, en recherchant à travers une grande variété d’étiquettes de genres différentes, ou en consultant nos listes de concerts locaux!

---

Pick A Piper (Toronto) is a collaborative live music project produced by Brad Weber with longtime pals Angus Fraser & Dan Roberts and many guest vocalists that combines polyrhythmic percussion, atmospheric sound design, loopy melodies, club-informed structures filled with feels with a focus on electronics and production technique to create a sound poised between the organic and the synthetic.

Loopsy Dazy (Montreal/Toronto) is a live-looping acoustic-electronic band consisting of Mikey Dorje on acoustic guitar, synths, beats, and effects, Eleanor Edgar on violin and effects, Brad Weber on drums and synth and Adam Jenkins on bass. Loopsy Dazy delights audiences and rocks dance floors with their unique symphony of sound that combines elements of both electronic and acoustic music.

Fall 2019 will see the release of Loopsy Dazy's debut album. The band's previous studio work includes a remix of a song by Austra for a video that was played at the 2014 Juno Awards, an official remix of electronic music pioneer BT (Brian Transeau), and other singles and collaborations.

descriptionHtml:

_______________________________________
GABRIELLE PAPILLON - Album Release, Shout
Shout is a triumph. It starts with the inner rumblings of the mind of an anxious person, someone who struggles with crowds and big groups of people, someone who craves solitude but does not really want to be left alone too long. It becomes the burst of energy and the surge of feeling that comes from the heart’s willingness to fight to be understood, to be less alone. Shout is propelled by equal parts synth, big piano, and anger, exploding in thoughtful, danceable art-pop anthems of uprising, hope and a delirious celebration of self.

I made Shout to share with the ones who are itching to bust out of their shells, of the boxes other people have built for them. For the awkward dancers, and the crowd-averse. For everyone who ever does anything brave even when it is hard. Whether it’s coming out, or reaching out to people you love who have shut you out. Whether it’s saying “Hey! I matter!” Whether it’s setting boundaries. It’s for the people who try new things even though it is terrifying, because they know it might end up being worth it.

I hope that you will like it. I do. But you know what? If you don’t, that’s okay, because I love it, and most days that will be enough. This is me at my very best yet and I am mightily proud of the journey chronicled here.
http://www.gabriellepapillon.com

With velvety, 80s-inspired layered synth and driving beats, Zinnia brings an explosive range to Cardiello's writing, equal parts intimate and fierce.
